clue.text: Therapeutic release from Prince: one big hit, backed by '60s group

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: backed means the word for a big hit is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: a slam is a heavy blow
Cream were the 1960s rock trio of Clapton, Bruce and Baker

explanation.surface: A therapy session is likened to a hit record by Prince, given backing by a sixties band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns only SLAM, giving MALS. Primal Scream are a Glasgow band, and Glasgow musicians are the puzzle's theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Primal therapy has the patient let out pent-up pain through cries, so this is a kind of cathartic outburst.

clue.text: The Queen's crazy about baked goods

indicators.note: about means the word for crazy goes round the royal letters

parts.note: potty is British slang for mad
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: The monarch is wild about cakes and bread.
explanation.walkthrough: ER = Elizabeth Regina, the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceramics are fired in a kiln, so clay wares are literally baked items.

clue.text: Sort of column written by 10 taking 13

parts.note: the figures 1 and 0 written out look like the letters I and O

indicators.note: 13-across is a short cut, so the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: nicking is stealing, so taking can be nick

explanation.surface: A newspaper column penned by the Glaswegian of 10-across, who borrows a shortcut.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' looks like a reference to GLASWEGIAN but is read as the characters I and O; '13' (SHORT CUT) tells you to cut NICK short to NIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Ionic is one of the classical orders of Greek architecture, with scroll-shaped capitals on its pillars.

clue.text: 17 Mar? Going topless, drink up

definitions.note: 17-down is a gas, and this answer is an example of one

indicators.note: going topless means the word Mar loses its first letter
in a down clue, up means the word for drink is read from bottom to top

parts.note: nog is a strong ale or eggnog

explanation.surface: A March day of going topless and downing drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: Argon is a noble gas, hence the cross-reference to 17-down.
explanation.definitionFit: It is one of the inert noble elements, a colourless gas making up about one percent of air.

clue.text: See 1
Sort of builder's bum primarily seen in women only, extremely firm on top

indicators.note: in a down clue, on top places the firm's letters first

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: seen in means the bum's letter sits inside the other letters
extremely means only the outer letters of only are used
primarily means the first letter of bum

explanation.surface: A builder's backside spotted on a women-only site, with the boss of the company looking down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes OY from 'only'; B goes between W and OY. A cowboy builder is British slang for a shoddy, unqualified tradesman.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a rogue tradesman doing cheap, botched work is called by this Wild West term.

clue.text: Cooked breakfast for one? Good

parts.note: eg, exempli gratia, means for example or for one

explanation.surface: Asking whether a fry-up for one is any good.
explanation.definitionFit: A boiled or fried one from a hen is a classic morning meal on its own.

clue.text: Tip from Midge Ure about each second bar of music

indicators.note: about means the outer letters go round the abbreviations for each and second
the tip from a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A musical tip from Midge Ure, the Glasgow-born Ultravox singer, about every second bar.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a measure is the American term for a bar, the group of beats between bar lines.

clue.text: Young female dog

definitions.meaning: a Scots word for a girl
the collie of the ... films and TV series

explanation.surface: A young girl dog, a puppy bitch.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the Scots word for a girl, and also the name of the famous fictional rough collie.

clue.text: "Short dwarf" shock

indicators.note: short means the word for dwarf loses its last letter

parts.note: to stunt growth is to dwarf it

explanation.surface: A short dwarf's surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dwarf' is a verb here, not a little person.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun someone is to daze or astonish them, as a shock does.

clue.text: Scot going on vacation around Wales upset a fellow countryman?

indicators.note: around means the outer letters of going go round the jumbled letters
on vacation means going is emptied, leaving only its outer letters
upset means the letters of Wales are disordered

parts.note: Ian is a typical Scottish man's name, a fellow Scot

explanation.surface: A Scot on holiday round Wales offends a compatriot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on vacation' is a common signal to empty a word, keeping only its ends; 'upset' signals the shuffle of the country's name. Ian stands for any Scotsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Glasgow is necessarily a Scot, so the definition names the wider group.

clue.text: Clergyman taking care of unhappy group

indicators.note: taking means the clergyman's title holds the abbreviation inside it

parts.note: a dean is a senior cleric
c/o, CO, is the postal abbreviation for care of
blue means sad

explanation.surface: A clergyman looking after a depressed congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: Deacon Blue are a Glasgow pop band. 'Clergyman' suggests a definition (deacon) but is only DEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a Scottish pop band, so it is a musical ensemble.

clue.text: 6s done, we're told

definitions.note: 6-down is a hen's product; plural here

indicators.note: we're told signals that the word is heard, not seen

parts.note: over means finished

explanation.surface: Six times finished, so people say.
explanation.definitionFit: Ova is the Latin plural for reproductive cells laid by females, the plural of 6-down's answer.

clue.text: Quick way to get to number 1?

definitions.meaning: a number 1 is the closest setting on hair clippers, giving a very cropped style

explanation.surface: Asking for the fastest route to the top of the charts.
explanation.definitionFit: A quicker route is a short cut, and a crop with clippers on the number 1 guard is a very short haircut.

clue.text: Clue about Lulu stripping? It's a bloomer

indicators.note: about means the hint goes round the stripped name

parts.note: a tip is a hint or clue

indicators.note: stripping takes the outer letters off Lulu

explanation.surface: A hint that Lulu, the Glasgow-born singer, is undressing: what a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' looks like a mistake but means a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer is a flowering plant, and the tulip is a classic spring bulb flower.

clue.text: Called into Greater Manchester town with a flowering shrub

indicators.note: into means the word for called goes inside the town

parts.note: Hyde is a town east of Manchester
rang means telephoned

explanation.surface: Someone phoned a Manchester town about a bush.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a garden bush with big round heads of blue, pink or white blossoms.

clue.text: Quickly make an approach

definitions.meaning: to ... curtains is to sew them in a hurry
the lead-in run before a jump or bowl, or the period before an event

explanation.surface: Making a quick approach to something.
explanation.definitionFit: To run something up is to make it hastily, and a run-up is the build-up or approach.

clue.text: 13 for rabbit

parts.note: 13-across reads as cut made short: gash, a cut, loses its last letter, and the result is slang for chatter, as rabbit is in British rhyming slang (rabbit and pork, talk)

explanation.surface: Taking a shortcut on account of a rabbit.
explanation.walkthrough: Written as a whole-clue reading because the cross-reference 13 does two jobs at once: CUT supplies GASH and SHORT trims its last letter, so no one word can be split between leaf and signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Both rabbit and this word are British slang verbs for idle, lengthy chatter.

clue.text: Warm and dry current in 3

indicators.note: in means the electrical symbol goes inside the chemical symbol

parts.note: 3-down's element has the chemical symbol Ar
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A hot, dry current in a reference to 3-down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' looks like part of the weather picture but is just I.
explanation.definitionFit: To air laundry is to hang it to finish drying and freshen it in warmth.

clue.text: See 11
Film of a Parisian

parts.note: in French de, shortened to d' before a vowel, means of
une is French for a

explanation.surface: A movie about a woman from Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parisian' signals French: d'une means of a.
explanation.definitionFit: It names the Frank Herbert science-fiction story filmed by David Lynch and later Denis Villeneuve.

clue.text: See 25
Torture to start with, private parts getting rejected at a party

indicators.note: getting rejected means the private initial and parts together are turned back to front
to start with picks the first letter of private

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: Torture whose first step is having one's private parts spurned at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting rejected' turns P plus PARTS into STRAPP.
explanation.definitionFit: Strappado was an old punishment hoisting a victim by the wrists tied behind them, then dropping them.

clue.text: Sitarist Ravi Shankar's group

indicators.note: the 's reads as has, so the letters are held within the musician's name

explanation.surface: The band of the Indian sitar maestro Ravi Shankar.
explanation.walkthrough: Travis are a Glasgow rock band.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs to a Scottish rock band, so it is a musical ensemble.

clue.text: Letter from broadband provider turned up

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the abbreviation is read from the bottom

parts.note: ISP is short for internet service provider

explanation.surface: A letter arriving from the broadband company.
explanation.definitionFit: Psi is the twenty-third letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Star wearing flower's a hippie icon

indicators.note: wearing means the river holds the star inside it, like clothing

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river; the Don is a river
a nova is a star that suddenly brightens

explanation.surface: A celebrity with a bloom on, the picture of a flower child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is a river, something that flows. Donovan is a Glasgow-born folk singer of the 1960s.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish singer of Mellow Yellow was a figurehead of the flower-power era.

clue.text: Musician playing online finished before mounting horse

indicators.note: playing means the letters of online are moved about

parts.note: done means finished

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounting means the word for horse climbs, reading upwards

parts.note: a nag is an old horse

explanation.surface: A performer streaming online, done before getting on a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' turns ONLINE into LONNIE; 'mounting' turns NAG into GAN. Lonnie Donegan, the Glasgow-born king of skiffle.
explanation.definitionFit: The skiffle star of Rock Island Line was a singer and guitarist, so a performer of songs.

clue.text: A short sleep at hotel, or before a part of the Eucharist

parts.note: a nap is a brief sleep
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Having a nap at a hotel, or before going to Mass.
explanation.definitionFit: The anaphora is the central eucharistic prayer of consecration in the liturgy.

clue.text: Policeman covering one location

indicators.note: covering means the musician's name goes round the numeral

parts.note: Sting was the singer of The Police
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A police officer guarding one spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Policeman' is not a constable but a member of the band The Police.
explanation.definitionFit: Siting means positioning or placement, the choice of where something stands.

clue.text: Blur start off Simple Minds' No.1 on the organ

indicators.note: start off picks the opening letter of Simple
No.1 picks the leading letter of Minds, its first in line

parts.note: the ear is the organ of hearing

explanation.surface: The band Blur kicks off, with Simple Minds' top hit in your ears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blur' looks like the Britpop band, but is a verb. Simple Minds are a Glasgow band.
explanation.definitionFit: To smudge or smear something is to blur its outline.

clue.text: Group of Scots, perhaps with back-up guitar

indicators.note: with means the reversed instrument replaces the same letters

parts.note: scot is an old word for a tax, so scots are taxes

indicators.note: in a down clue, back-up means the word for guitar reads upwards

parts.note: axe is slang for a guitar

explanation.surface: A Scottish band, perhaps, with a backing guitarist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scots' are not people but old levies (scot, as in scot-free); 'back-up' turns the guitar word round inside them. Texas are a Glasgow band.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs to a Scottish pop-rock band fronted by Sharleen Spiteri.

clue.text: Exaggerate unusually daring gaze

indicators.note: unusually means the letters of daring gaze appear in an odd order

explanation.surface: Making too much of a strikingly bold stare.
explanation.definitionFit: To aggrandize something is to make it seem greater than it is, to inflate or overstate it.

clue.text: Run away with heart of mystery shopper

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
A stands for away in football results

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its centre letter

explanation.surface: A shopper running off with the key to a mystery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shopper' is not a customer but someone who shops (informs on) others.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are slang for an informer who betrays people to the authorities.

clue.text: Footballer's acceleration during 16

indicators.note: during means the physics symbol goes within the numeral

parts.note: XVI is sixteen in Roman numerals
a is the physics symbol for acceleration

explanation.surface: A footballer's burst of speed in his sixteenth minute.
explanation.walkthrough: '16' looks like a cross-reference to 16-down but is XVI.
explanation.definitionFit: Xavi Hernandez was the Barcelona and Spain midfielder.

clue.text: Head girl gets kick between her legs?

parts.note: nut is slang for head
Meg is a girl's name

explanation.definitionFit: In football a nutmeg is putting the ball through an opponent's legs.

clue.text: Confiteor is one's prayer

indicators.note: the 's reads as has, so the phrase holds the letters within it
